annotation.title_clean: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.title_en: Robot-First Mars Settlement: A Conceptual Framework for Technology Governance, Risk Reduction, and Interplanetary Policy
annotation.venue: Innovation Journal of Social Sciences and Economic Review
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual journal article proposing a robot-first Mars settlement phase, in which a swarm of about 10,000 autonomous AI robots tests infrastructure and failure recovery before humans arrive. It stresses AI governance, human oversight, accountability, planetary protection and compliance with international space law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous robot swarms should be deployed as a preparatory phase before human arrival on Mars.
Controlled failure can become operational learning, reducing uncertainty in settlement planning.
Robot-first colonization complements rather than replaces human settlement ambitions.
Governance needs human oversight, accountability, planetary protection and compliance with space law.
The framework rests on literature synthesis and scenario analysis, with no empirical data.
